excluded.reason: Gamification and internal-only Google code paths in the shipped backend: implementation trivia with no product relevance for Verevon.
Transcript search in a worker thread: an implementation detail of a local desktop store; conversation search belongs to the chat-core category.
Legacy ChatGPT agent/Operator, retired; superseded by records in other clusters.
Vendor speed/quality benchmark claims (marketing), not a capability.
Enterprise Workflows retired and migrated to Skills; no runtime capability left (skills belong to the extensibility category).

clusters.name: Typed step/turn model and loop state machine
clusters.description: Every turn is a sequence of typed, status-bearing steps or items (model response, tool call, user input, checkpoint, system message) with explicit phase transitions, a closed turn-end vocabulary and a canonical event taxonomy, so the UI, replay, cancel, fork and revert can all act on one model.

bestInClass.why: DeepSeek (q5, SRC) makes each request a pure function of an append-only log with documented interception points and exactly one logged turn-end reason; Antigravity's 118-type step enum (q5) is the richest step vocabulary. Together they give replayable, inspectable turns.

clusters.mechanism: Persist an append-only log of typed records per run: step{id, run_id, ordinal, kind(enum), status(pending|running|done|error|cancelled), source, started_at, ended_at, payload}. Build each model request as a pure fold over the log (prompt reconciliation, admission of queued input, tool history). Close every turn with exactly one reason (completed, max_rounds, max_tokens, cancelled, tool_concluded, error). Emit the same records as SSE events with a monotonic id so live UI, resume and replay share one source. Reject events whose turn id is not the active one (T3 lifecycle guard).

verevon.gap: Verevon has append-only runs/events rows, a 23-variant typed SSE ChatEvent taxonomy and managed terminal receipts. Weaker: no single closed turn-end vocabulary shared by both loops, and request building is not a pure fold of the log (two loops kept by decision).
verevon.strengths: Typed SSE taxonomy CI-checked against the SPA, durable replay via /v1/runs/:id/events, terminalization receipts with finalization_pending instead of fake success. Keep the gateway as a byte-verbatim pipe.

clusters.benefit: Already in place; a closed turn-end vocabulary would let the Work panel and evals branch on outcomes reliably.
clusters.approach: Add a TurnEndReason enum to mp-contracts, emitted by both loops in the terminal receipt; no loop unification (HARN-1/2 rejected).
clusters.risks: Low; must not reopen the rejected loop-unification decision.
clusters.rationale: Verevon is roughly at parity; only polish remains.

clusters.name: Loop budgets and termination controls
clusters.description: Explicit caps on model invocations, rounds, tokens and wall-clock time, with a reserved concluding call and a visible card when a run stops on budget.

bestInClass.why: Antigravity's executor config (q5) exposes max invocations, forced continuations, terminal step types and require-finish-tool; Manus turns budget exhaustion into a 'may be stuck' card with Continue.

clusters.mechanism: Resolve a budget server-side per run {max_rounds, max_tokens, wall_clock_s, max_children}; when the next round would exceed it, run one concluding no-tool round so the user still gets an answer; surface the stop reason as a typed event that the UI renders with a Continue action starting a new budgeted run.

verevon.gap: Budgets, concluding round and wall-clock guard are shipped. Missing: a user-facing 'stopped on budget, continue?' card; and the 300 s delegated bearer (OD8) bounds every run regardless of budget.
verevon.strengths: Server-resolved budget never taken from the client, atomic shared subagent budget, concluding round. Keep.

clusters.benefit: A Continue card makes budget stops recoverable instead of looking like failures.
clusters.approach: Emit a budget_exhausted terminal reason and render a Continue card in ChatMessages; handle OD8 with the goals work (C34).
clusters.risks: Continue must re-resolve the budget server-side and never trust client counts.
clusters.rationale: Parity on mechanics; only a small UX addition.

clusters.name: Mid-turn steering and message queueing
clusters.description: While the agent works, the user can queue a follow-up, steer the running turn, or interrupt; messages have delivery states and survive connection loss.

bestInClass.why: Claude (q5) runs a delivery state machine with held steers, deferred sends and replay after loss; DeepSeek uses one durable inbox with next-turn/next-step targets and a wake flag.

clusters.mechanism: Durable inbox per run {message_id, target next_step|next_turn, state queued|delivered|refused}; delivered at the next tool-round boundary; echo uuids for idempotency; held across disconnects and replayed; UI shows pending/delivered/refused.

verevon.gap: Baseline narrative: POST /v1/invoke/:id/queue delivers at the next tool-round boundary and the model classifies the pause (shipped), shown as pending/delivered/refused in the SPA. The queue registry is in-memory and single-replica, so queued input is lost on restart or another replica.
verevon.strengths: The 'pause the model classifies' semantics is an owner decision more nuanced than steer/followUp.

clusters.benefit: Reliability under multi-replica deploys.
clusters.approach: Move the queued-input registry to session-core (durable inbox rows keyed by run) or Redis like the stream buffer.
clusters.risks: Ordering across replicas.
clusters.rationale: Feature shipped; durability is the gap.

clusters.name: Interrupt semantics and tool-history repair
clusters.description: Stopping a run keeps the text the user already saw, closes unanswered tool calls with explicit outcomes (aborted, not started, unknown), and confirms before stopping work that cannot resume.

bestInClass.why: DeepSeek (q5, SRC) records the delivered prefix as an interrupted assistant message and always repairs paired tool history; Hermes closes failed turns with a system-authored row.

clusters.mechanism: On cancel: persist delivered text/reasoning as assistant{interrupted:true}; for each tool call without a result append ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH, TOOL_NOT_STARTED or TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (telling the model to retry only idempotent work); close the turn with reason cancelled.

verevon.gap: Cooperative stop/cancel is shipped (baseline narrative, cancel_registry.rs, in-memory). Not verified: persistence of the partial assistant text and synthetic results for unanswered tool calls after cancel.
verevon.strengths: Cancel is bound to tenant, user and run; unconfirmed cancels are reconciled in the SPA.

clusters.benefit: Follow-ups after Stop stay coherent; effectful calls with unknown outcome are not blindly retried.
clusters.approach: Check session_flow.rs; if missing, add interrupted-message persistence and tool-history closers in both loops.
clusters.risks: Retrying an effect with unknown outcome; tie to C22.

clusters.name: Durable execution, crash recovery and continuation
clusters.description: Runs survive process crashes, restarts and approval pauses: work is made durable before effects, a lease prevents double writers, interrupted runs resume automatically and an approved pause continues the agent loop.

bestInClass.why: DeepSeek (q4, SRC) checkpoints before model requests, tool effects and next steps and repairs the tail on cold resume; Hermes holds a refreshed turn lease with a stall watchdog; Cursor auto-continues interrupted agents and delivers questions durably.

clusters.mechanism: Persist before each model call and before each effectful tool; on resume take write ownership (lease row with heartbeat), append crash closers for interrupted calls, then rebuild the request from the log and continue; an approval decision re-enters the same loop with the saved state instead of only re-executing the approved effect.

verevon.gap: Terminalization receipts, recovery worker, drain on redeploy and stream resume are shipped. Missing: after an approval the LLM loop does not resume reasoning (only 3 effect types are re-executed from an encrypted descriptor), the descriptor key is empty on the stack so pauses return unavailable, and there is no resume of an interrupted mid-run loop.
verevon.strengths: Exact-effect descriptor with postcondition check is a safer primitive than most sources have.

clusters.benefit: Blocks the agent vision: an approval that does not continue the task, or a crash that loses it, breaks trust in Do mode.
clusters.approach: Persist loop state (log fold inputs) in session-core at each round; on approval or crash, a continuation worker in execution-core re-enters run_rounds from the saved state under the original grant; configure SESSION_CORE_CONTINUATION_DESCRIPTOR_KEY.
clusters.risks: Double execution if the lease is wrong; authority re-check required at resume (Control reauthorizer).
clusters.rationale: Core reliability gap for every agentic flow.

clusters.name: Exactly-once side effects (action ledger)
clusters.description: Each effectful tool call carries a stable action id; a ledger keyed by session and action with a payload digest replays the stored result instead of repeating the effect.

bestInClass.why: Only source (q5, SRC): (sessionUid, actionId) key, payload digest and a 10-minute replay horizon.

clusters.mechanism: For non-read side-effect classes compute key = hash(run_id, action_id); if a completed row exists with the same digest return the stored result; if digests differ refuse; otherwise execute and store; expire after a replay horizon.

verevon.gap: Idempotent send/regenerate registry (in-memory), keyed-MAC start keys, and exact-effect descriptors with postconditions exist; no general per-tool-call action ledger for provider writes was found.
verevon.strengths: Postcondition verification after effects is stronger than a ledger alone.

clusters.benefit: Safe retries and resumes for provider writes (Visma, mail, shipping).
clusters.approach: Add an action ledger table in execution-core keyed by (run_id, tool_call_id) with payload digest, consulted before execute_provider_action.
clusters.risks: Low; storage growth.
clusters.rationale: Small table, large safety gain for C21.

clusters.name: Provider and stream retry with error taxonomy and failover
clusters.description: Model-call and stream failures are classified into typed reasons with recovery hints, retried with backoff and jitter, failed over to another route or model, and parked with a visible countdown when exhausted.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q4) classifies about 30 failover reasons with recovery flags and parks exhausted turns with a countdown; Codex reconnects visibly and can switch model per step; Cursor detects stalled streams.

clusters.mechanism: classify(error) -> {reason, retryable, failover_ok, user_message}; exponential backoff with jitter; stall detector on the stream; failover chain across routes; when exhausted, park the turn with a resume-at time instead of failing.

verevon.gap: Tool-call retry (3 attempts) and prompt-too-long recovery are shipped. Check inference-core for a provider failover chain and stream stall detection; neither appears in the baseline.
verevon.strengths: Shared failure vocabulary pinned by a contract test.

clusters.benefit: Fewer user-visible failures on provider outages.
clusters.approach: Add a typed ProviderFailure enum and a route failover list in inference-core; park-and-resume via C21.
clusters.risks: Failover must respect ZDR-attested routes only.

clusters.name: User-facing typed error states and recovery actions
clusters.description: Failures are shown as specific cards by error class (quota, credits, engine crash, sandbox failure) with targeted recovery actions such as retry, refund-aware retry or 'try fixing'.

bestInClass.why: Claude (q5) classifies engine/stream/network failures into targeted messages; Antigravity separates user and model error messages; Manus offers refund-aware retry.

clusters.mechanism: Error event {class, user_message, model_message, retryable, actions[]}; UI maps classes to cards; model-visible message differs from the user one.

verevon.gap: Error recovery for interrupted and unresumable turns is shipped; no refund-aware or credit-specific cards were found in the baseline.
verevon.strengths: Durable-outcome reconciliation when a stream cannot resume.

clusters.benefit: Polish.
clusters.approach: Add credit/quota error classes once Control-plane billing exposes them.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Capacity- and credit-aware run admission (queue, pause, resume)
clusters.description: When capacity or credits run out, tasks wait in a queue with an estimate or pause instead of failing, and resume automatically when credits return.

bestInClass.why: Perplexity (q4, DOC) pauses rather than cancels on credit exhaustion; Manus (q4, SRC) shows per-tier wait estimates and alternatives.

clusters.mechanism: Before each round check the cost reservation; on shortfall set run status paused_for_credit and persist state; a billing event resumes it; at admission show queue position or a cheaper tier.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Check Control-plane billing and Model-plane cost reservation (proposal section 18 is listed as not built).

clusters.benefit: Long runs do not die on a credit boundary.
clusters.approach: Implement after C21 (needs resumable state) with Control-plane billing events.
clusters.risks: Billing correctness.

clusters.name: Loop hygiene: repetition, no-progress and stop gates
clusters.description: The runtime detects repeated text, identical failing tool calls and no-progress cycles, nudges or stops the model, recovers from output-limit or empty responses, and can turn a premature prose answer into another iteration.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q4) runs a side-effect-free controller for repeat, cycle and no-progress detection plus stop gates; Cursor detects streamed text repetition; DeepSeek escalates reminders at 3, 5 and 8 repeats.

clusters.mechanism: Keep a rolling window of (tool, args hash, result class); on N identical failing calls or no new information inject an escalating reminder, then stop with a loop reason; a streaming detector for repeated lines (code-fence aware); bounded retry on empty or max-tokens responses with a note to the model.

verevon.gap: Only the truncated final tool call in a length-stopped message is refused (shipped). No repetition or no-progress detector found (SRC grep for repeat/loop guard found none); loop-family stall detection is a proposal (MODEL_PLANE_IMPROVEMENTS section 21).
verevon.strengths: Precise handling of length-stopped tool calls.

clusters.benefit: Saves tokens and avoids stuck runs, which users notice as 'it keeps doing the same thing'.
clusters.approach: Add a LoopGuard in mp-contracts used by both loops: args-hash window plus reminder ladder; emit a typed loop_detected end reason.
clusters.risks: False positives on legitimate polling.
clusters.rationale: Small, high-value guard present in three strong harnesses.

clusters.name: Tool execution pipeline: validation, repair, timeouts and typed failures
clusters.description: Tool arguments are validated strictly, malformed JSON is repaired, calls have deadlines, and failures carry a type plus separate user-visible and model-visible messages.

bestInClass.why: Cursor (q5) has a typed tool-failure taxonomy with split client/model messages and argument repair; Antigravity validates strictly with per-call timeouts.

clusters.mechanism: validate(args, schema) before dispatch; repair common JSON faults; enforce declared timeout via cancellation; failures typed {invalid_args, timeout, user_rejected, provider_error, ...} with a short UI message and an actionable model message.

verevon.gap: Schema validation, MCP argument repair and argument grounding are shipped. Not verified: split user/model failure messages and per-tool deadlines.
verevon.strengths: The grounding gate that refuses fabricated user-only arguments is beyond the reference sources.

clusters.benefit: Keep.
clusters.approach: Optionally add split messages to the shared failure vocabulary.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Streaming tool execution overlapped with generation
clusters.description: Tool calls start executing as soon as their arguments finish streaming, while the model is still generating later output.

bestInClass.why: Only source (q5, SRC): a tee on the model stream dispatches each completed tool call immediately.

clusters.mechanism: Tee the provider stream; accumulate text into the assistant message; on tool-call-complete dispatch read-only calls immediately (effectful calls still wait for the gate); guard duplicate ids; join results before the next round.

verevon.gap: The tool phase streams, but dispatch appears to happen after the response completes (join_all per round). Check tool_loop.rs for early dispatch.

clusters.benefit: Lower latency on multi-tool rounds.
clusters.approach: Early-dispatch read-only tools only; keep effectful calls behind the capability gate.
clusters.risks: Executing calls from a response that is later cancelled.

clusters.name: Safe parallel tool scheduling
clusters.description: Independent tool calls in one response run concurrently with a cap, while interactive or side-effecting calls act as barriers and path-conflicting calls are serialized.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q5) splits a batch into ordered parallel and sequential segments by path scope; DeepSeek runs a fail-closed bounded scheduler (default 10).

clusters.mechanism: Classify each call (read-only, effectful, interactive); group consecutive read-only calls without path overlap into parallel segments; effectful/interactive calls are barriers; serialize approval prompts; cap concurrency.

verevon.gap: Parallel dispatch with join_all in both loops is shipped with an atomic shared subagent budget. Not found: barrier semantics for effectful calls within a batch or a concurrency cap.
verevon.strengths: Adopted from DeepSeek's executionMode idea with a shared budget.

clusters.benefit: Mostly at parity.
clusters.approach: Add effectful-call barriers to the dispatcher (is_risky_call already exists).
clusters.risks: Ordering bugs on concurrent provider writes.

clusters.name: Large tool output spill to files or handles
clusters.description: Oversized tool output is replaced by a head/tail preview and a reference to the full content that the agent can search or read later.

bestInClass.why: DeepSeek (q4) spills to private 0700 files with opaque locators inside a shared token budget; Hermes adds a per-turn budget.

clusters.mechanism: If output > max_inline_tokens, store full text as a run-scoped blob, return {preview_head, marker, preview_tail, handle, size}; a read/query tool fetches ranges from the handle; blobs expire with the run (and are never stored on ZDR turns).

verevon.gap: Baseline narrative: large MCP results become queryable handles (result_query). Not found for built-in tools (fetch_url, knowledge, provider actions).
verevon.strengths: Result handles already exist as a primitive.

clusters.benefit: Protects the context window in Do runs that read large documents or exports.
clusters.approach: Generalize ToolResultHandle to every tool result above a threshold in both loops.
clusters.risks: ZDR: handles must not persist on ZDR turns.

clusters.name: Deferred tool loading and tool search
clusters.description: Tool schemas are not all sent up front; the model searches for tools by name or description and loads only those it needs.

bestInClass.why: Codex (q5) ranks tools with BM25 and supports direct vs deferred exposure; Antigravity loads MCP tools lazily; Manus starts lean and loads capabilities on demand.

clusters.mechanism: Expose a tool_search{query,limit} tool returning names and schemas; mark tools direct or deferred per server; loaded tools join the offered set for the rest of the run.

verevon.gap: Baseline narrative: above 40 MCP tools the catalogue collapses to mcp_catalog + mcp_call. But MCP tools are not invocable by either loop (capability gate denies mcp__*), so this is not effective today.
verevon.strengths: Staged disclosure already designed.

clusters.benefit: Only valuable once MCP invocation works.
clusters.approach: Fix the MCP capability binding first (extensibility category), then extend staged disclosure to built-in tool families.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Lifecycle hooks around tools, prompts and sessions
clusters.description: User-, admin- or plugin-defined handlers run before and after tool calls, model calls, prompts, compaction and stop, and can allow, deny, rewrite input or inject context.

bestInClass.why: Cursor (q5) wraps every tool call with generic and tool-specific pre/post hooks; Antigravity has a JSON contract with step injection; Codex supports command, MCP-tool and agent handlers.

clusters.mechanism: Hook registry {event, matcher, handler(command|http|prompt), timeout}; pre-hooks return allow|deny|ask plus optional rewritten input and additional context; post-hooks can append context; durable store with per-org admin rules.

verevon.gap: The engine is real (allow/deny/ask, glob match) but rules live in an in-memory registry, are passed only on browser runs, and the Do loop passes an empty hook_context; no durable store, UI or input rewrite.
verevon.strengths: Hook decisions compose with the capability gate.

clusters.benefit: Org admins can enforce policy (e.g. block sending mail outside the domain) without code changes.
clusters.approach: Persist hook rules in capability-core per org/Space, pass hook_context into Do runs, add a settings UI; handlers limited to declarative rules plus HTTP webhooks (no shell in a web product).
clusters.risks: Hooks must never widen authority, only narrow it.
clusters.rationale: Engine exists; wiring is the gap.

clusters.name: Cache-stable prompt architecture and ephemeral context
clusters.description: The system prompt stays byte-stable for a conversation; changing facts (time, environment, memory recall, reminders) are appended as sourced deltas or wire-only sidecars, so provider prefix caches keep hitting.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q5) makes prefix-cache stability an invariant governing all mid-conversation injection and replays wire-only context byte-identically; DeepSeek (q5) appends runtime facts only when they change; Manus published the KV-cache lessons.

clusters.mechanism: Order prompt as stable, context, volatile tiers; never rewrite earlier messages; append runtime-context snapshots as sourced messages only on change; attach per-turn recall as a wire-only sidecar stored alongside the turn so replays are byte-identical; place provider cache breakpoints at tier boundaries; measure cache-hit ratio per route.

verevon.gap: Anthropic cache_control breakpoints exist in inference-core (SRC, grep). Baseline narrative: prompt-cache hits were never measured on any route and the OpenAI-route items are undeployed. No invariant governing mid-conversation injection was found.
verevon.strengths: Cache-read tokens are displayed when present.

clusters.benefit: Lower cost and latency per turn; important for the Verevon Balance cost model.
clusters.approach: Define a prompt-tier contract in mp-contracts, add a cache-hit metric per route, and move volatile injections (time, recall, skills) to an append-only tail.
clusters.risks: ZDR routes may disallow provider caching; caching must respect ZDR propagation.
clusters.rationale: Direct cost lever, moderate effort, invisible to users.

clusters.name: Structured prompt assembly and run context seeding
clusters.description: The prompt is assembled from named sections and structured context blocks (environment, rules, instruction files, attachments, history) with per-model gating and entry-point-aware variants, so every run starts with the right context.

bestInClass.why: Cursor (q5) builds the system prompt as a component tree with per-model gating and a typed RequestContext with hydration flags; DeepSeek loads a workspace instruction chain with a byte budget.

clusters.mechanism: Sections as typed components rendered to role messages; a typed request context {thread_history, persona, org/Space instructions, memory prefetch, attachments, environment} assembled server-side with completeness flags; per-turn XML-tagged blocks; entry-point variants (web, scheduled, channel).

verevon.gap: Do-mode runs start with a fresh history: preamble plus goal (plus skills, plus approved plan). No prior thread turns, no persona, org or Space instructions and no memory prefetch (agent.rs:1185-1200, sse.rs:9135-9150). Plain chat does assemble context.

clusters.benefit: Blocks the product vision: a Do run that ignores the conversation and the org's instructions feels broken to users immediately.
clusters.approach: Reuse Session Core GetContextAssembly (already used by the context inspector) to seed Do runs with thread history, persona and org/Space instructions, under the same compaction budget; keep Space ACLs (never widen) and ZDR (no persisted seed on ZDR turns).
clusters.risks: Context bloat in a 4-round budget; must not leak Space content beyond the run's lease.
clusters.rationale: Highest-impact gap in this category; moderate effort using existing parts.

clusters.name: Host activity ledger and human-change awareness
clusters.description: The host tells the agent about events it did not cause (rewinds, user edits, files changed by a person) as clearly framed, escaped non-instruction context.

bestInClass.why: Claude (q5) drains an activity ledger into a tagged, escaped block framed as information, not instructions; Cursor tracks what the human changed since the last read.

clusters.mechanism: Per-thread ledger of host events {kind, at, summary}; drained at the next user turn into a <host-activity since=...> block with tag escaping and an explicit 'this is not an instruction' frame.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Check whether Do/chat runs are told when a user edited an artifact or Space document between turns.

clusters.benefit: Avoids the agent overwriting user edits to artifacts or Space files; also a prompt-injection defence pattern.
clusters.approach: Application Plane change events projected into a ledger the gateway drains per turn.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Context compaction core (prune, summarize, provider-native)
clusters.description: When the window fills, old tool results are pruned without a model call, then the middle of the history is summarized (same model, auxiliary model or provider-native compaction), with a manual trigger.

bestInClass.why: Cursor (q5) combines self-summary that keeps the cache prefix, vendor-native compaction and background summarisation; Codex (q5) has a trigger taxonomy and server-side compaction v2; Hermes and DeepSeek prune tool output before any summary.

clusters.mechanism: Two-stage reduction: (1) model-free pruning of old tool results to head/marker/tail; (2) summarize the middle with protected head and tail, using provider-native compaction when available and the local summarizer as fallback; record usage separately; trigger proactively at a threshold and reactively on a provider overflow error.

verevon.gap: Both loops compact; the Do loop has tier 1 only (no head summary). Native Anthropic clear_tool_uses and server compaction are wired, but local compaction always runs as well.
verevon.strengths: Tiered compaction, provider-native editing, prompt-too-long recovery and protected pins are at parity with the best sources.

clusters.benefit: Already strong.
clusters.approach: Add tier 2 (head summary) to the Do loop when Do runs gain thread history (C18b).
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Compaction robustness (transactions, breakers, deterministic fallback, background summarization)
clusters.description: Compaction is a recorded transaction that either completes or leaves a detectable lock; failures arm a cooldown and fall back to deterministic truncation; summaries can be computed in the background and committed only if needed.

bestInClass.why: DeepSeek (q5) records compaction as a bracket transaction and rejects non-shrinking summaries; Cursor (q5) runs summarization in the background and persists or discards at turn end; Hermes adds an anti-thrash breaker.

clusters.mechanism: compaction/start record, summarize, revalidate that the span did not change, reject summaries that do not shrink, then append compaction/commit; on repeated failure arm a persisted cooldown ladder and fall back to deterministic max-min fair truncation with an honest marker; optionally start the summary early in the background.

verevon.gap: A failed summary degrades to truncation with an honest marker (test in compaction.rs). Not found: a recorded bracket transaction, an anti-thrash cooldown, background pre-computation.
verevon.strengths: Honest-marker truncation fallback exists.

clusters.benefit: Prevents compaction loops and silent context loss on long Do runs.
clusters.approach: Persist compaction start/commit rows in session-core and add a cooldown counter per thread.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Compaction fidelity (framing, verbatim user messages, warm prefix, recall)
clusters.description: Techniques that keep what matters after compaction: reference-only summary framing, verbatim user messages, cache-warm summarizer requests, skill markers, recall tools and progress notes before a window reset.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q5) frames the summary as reference-only with clauses learned from real failures and keeps user messages verbatim in lean mode; DeepSeek (q5) replays the conversation's own system prompt and tools so the summarizer call hits the cache.

clusters.mechanism: Summary prefix states it is background and that the latest user message wins; keep all user messages verbatim plus a mechanical anchor index; send the summarizer the same system prompt and tool declarations to reuse the cache; demote large skill bodies to markers listed in the summary; give the model a tool to re-read dropped turns.

verevon.gap: reattach_context/reattach_skill, protected pins and a compaction-recall eval harness are shipped. Not verified: reference-only framing text and verbatim retention of user messages.
verevon.strengths: Need-driven reattachment plus a recall eval in CI is ahead of most sources, which have no recall measurement.

clusters.benefit: Keep.
clusters.approach: Add Hermes-style reference-only framing to the head summary prompt and a recall case for it.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Context-window transparency and manual compaction
clusters.description: A visible context meter with token breakdown and truncation reasons, plus a /compact command that reports saved tokens.

bestInClass.why: Claude (q4) shows a context ring with the auto-compact point and suggests compacting; Antigravity records truncation reasons per call; DeepSeek's /compact reports saved tokens.

clusters.mechanism: Per model call record {estimated_tokens, max_tokens, breakdown by source, truncation_reason}; UI ring with the auto-compact threshold; /compact runs a compaction outside a model turn and returns tokens saved.

verevon.gap: Baseline narrative: a context inspector (GET /v1/threads/:id/context with per-segment token estimates) is shipped and cache-read tokens appear in Work telemetry; a /compact command exists in the capability-core catalogue but no evidence the composer uses it.
verevon.strengths: Itemised context inspector is a DeepSeek-grade transparency feature.

clusters.benefit: Matches the 'maximum transparency' reference (DeepSeek).
clusters.approach: Wire /compact in the composer to CompactNow and show a context ring from the inspector data.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Plan mode with reviewable plan and approval gate
clusters.description: The agent researches read-only, produces a structured, editable plan, and executes only after the user approves; some products enforce the read-only phase server-side.

bestInClass.why: Codex (q5) requires one decision-complete proposed_plan after a read-only interview; Antigravity (q5) adds task boundaries with PLANNING/EXECUTION/VERIFICATION modes and plans only when warranted.

clusters.mechanism: Mode flag on the run; in planning mode refuse every risky/effectful call at dispatch (not only in prompt text); the model calls plan.propose{steps[], assumptions, risks} once; the UI renders an editable plan card (edit/reorder/remove/add, comments); approval mints a scoped autonomy grant and the approved plan is injected into the execution run, which then continues automatically.

verevon.gap: Server-side enforcement and the editable plan card are shipped. Missing: approving does not automatically continue the run (no SPA turn consumes the grant and edited plan; B7 planned), and the grant store is in memory.
verevon.strengths: Plan mode is enforced at dispatch regardless of posture, which is stronger than the prompt-only or advisory plan modes of Claude Code, DeepSeek and Cursor. Keep this.

clusters.benefit: Closing approve-then-continue makes Do mode feel like Manus or ChatGPT Work: one approval, then the agent runs.
clusters.approach: On plan approval, session-core persists the grant durably (thread-scoped carrier) and the gateway starts the execution run with the edited plan; the SPA shows the run continuing in place.
clusters.risks: The grant scope must never exceed the approved plan's authority rung.
clusters.rationale: Highly visible gap in a feature that is otherwise ahead.

clusters.name: Progress checklist (todo) tool and recitation
clusters.description: A lightweight model-maintained task list (pending/in_progress/completed) shown to the user and re-injected near the context tail so it survives compaction.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q4) keeps a revisioned todo store and re-injects it after compression; Codex keeps update_plan separate from Plan Mode with at most one item in progress.

clusters.mechanism: Tool todo_write{items[{id,content,status}]} replaces the whole list (single owner); store with a monotonic revision; after compaction or every N rounds append the current list as an ephemeral tail block (Manus todo recitation) instead of editing the system prompt.

verevon.gap: A durable plans/todos store and the Work-panel todo view exist; model-managed recitation into the context tail is planned, not built.
verevon.strengths: Todos are durable in session-core with tenant CAS.

clusters.benefit: Keeps long Do runs on track after compaction; cheap.
clusters.approach: Add a tail recitation block in both loops fed from orchestration_store todos; keep the prefix byte-stable.
clusters.risks: Must not break the prompt-cache prefix.

clusters.name: Blocking review requests with confidence and inline review comments
clusters.description: The agent asks for review of named artifacts with a confidence score and an auto-proceed flag; comments left on artifact selections or diffs are attached to the next turn.

bestInClass.why: Only source (q5, SRC): a typed notify_user step and ArtifactComment with approval status.

clusters.mechanism: Tool notify_user{artifact_refs[], blocking, confidence, justification, auto_proceed}; the UI lets the user comment on text selections in artifacts; comments are serialized as structured user-input parts {artifact_id, selection, comment, status approved|changes_requested} on the next turn.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Check the Frontend Plane artifact/canvas for selection comments and whether they flow into the next turn (canvas highlight-to-edit I17 is listed as planned).

clusters.benefit: Natural fit for Verevon artifacts (documents, decks): review by comment instead of retyping.
clusters.approach: Frontend: selection comments on artifacts; gateway: attach them as typed parts; Model: an optional notify tool in Do mode.
clusters.risks: Low.
clusters.rationale: Unique to one source; good for document work but not blocking.

clusters.name: Agent modes and mode switching
clusters.description: Named modes (ask, agent, plan, debug, autonomous) that the user or the model can switch between, with mode-specific prompts and nudges.

bestInClass.why: Cursor (q4) ships eight modes plus a mode-switch tool; Antigravity's autonomous mode removes questions and review gates.

clusters.mechanism: Mode enum on the turn; each mode selects a base prompt section and a tool allowlist; a switch_mode tool lets the model propose a change that the user confirms; a mode change injects a one-time nudge.

verevon.gap: The Ask/Do toggle and an autonomy ladder are shipped; there is no model-proposed mode switch.
verevon.strengths: An autonomy ladder (read_only < workspace_write < danger_full_access) checked per call is a cleaner model than many modes.

clusters.benefit: Minor.
clusters.approach: Optionally let the model propose Ask to Do through a typed suggestion card.
clusters.risks: Model-proposed escalation must stay user-confirmed.

clusters.name: Per-turn run overrides and mid-task model switching
clusters.description: Each turn can carry its own model, reasoning effort, approval policy and sandbox; the orchestrator model can change between follow-ups without restarting.

bestInClass.why: Codex's typed 27-field TurnStartParams (q5) is the most complete override envelope.

clusters.mechanism: Typed TurnStart{model, effort, approval_policy, sandbox_level, collaboration_mode, ...} validated server-side and clamped per surface and plan; thread-level defaults with per-turn overrides persisted on the run record.

verevon.gap: No baseline record in this category. Check model-gateway normalize.rs and the composer for per-turn model/effort fields and whether Do runs accept a mid-thread model change.

clusters.benefit: Lets users move a hard step to a stronger model without losing context.
clusters.approach: Extend the invoke request contract with typed per-turn overrides, clamped by Control-plane entitlements.
clusters.risks: Entitlement bypass if not clamped server-side.

clusters.name: Structured clarifying questions and human-in-the-loop requests
clusters.description: The agent pauses to ask a typed question (single/multi choice or free text), may continue independent work while waiting, and answers arrive durably even after the turn paused.

bestInClass.why: Manus (q5) routes all human requests as typed socket messages; Codex supports sync and async request_user_input; Cursor delivers late answers durably into the paused run.

clusters.mechanism: Tool ask_user{questions[{id, prompt, kind single|multi|text, options[]}], blocking, timeout_s}; the run records waiting_on_user_input; the UI renders a question card; the answer is stored and injected as a typed user-input part, resuming the run; on timeout the model is released to continue independent work.

verevon.gap: No clarify/ask-user tool found in model-gateway or execution-core (SRC grep for ask_user, request_user_input, ask_question: none). Only approval pauses exist (HITL approval cards).
verevon.strengths: The approval pause machinery (durable CreateApproval, awaiting_approval event) can be reused.

clusters.benefit: Users notice immediately when an agent guesses instead of asking; table-stakes in Manus, Codex, Cursor and ChatGPT Work.
clusters.approach: Add an ask_user tool to both loops that reuses the approval pause path (durable request row, SSE awaiting_input event, decide endpoint) and the C21 continuation to resume.
clusters.risks: Overuse; limit to Do mode or ambiguous goals via prompt rules.
clusters.rationale: Common across sources, absent in Verevon, reuses existing pause plumbing.

clusters.name: Action approvals and permission policy
clusters.description: Effectful actions require confirmation according to a policy; approval cards carry typed input; unattended sessions get reduced tools; forged approval cards are rejected.

bestInClass.why: Claude (q5) decides permissions in the host, rejects forged card-named tools and denies with clear messages in unattended runs; Manus attaches typed input schemas to confirmations.

clusters.mechanism: Host-side permission callback per call: deny tool names that imitate internal cards, apply surface gates, then policy allow|ask|deny; unattended runs start without tools that need a person; confirmation cards carry a schema for editable inputs.

verevon.gap: Approvals, capability gate with signed evidence, autonomy ladder and purpose-lock allowlist are shipped. Not found: editable typed inputs on approval cards and 'don't ask again' rules (open per CHD 13.3).
verevon.strengths: Every dispatch calls capability-core EvaluatePolicy; Allow needs Ed25519-signed evidence; unknown tools fail closed. This is ahead of all reference sources.

clusters.benefit: Keep.
clusters.approach: Add editable 'don't ask again' rules scoped per Space with audit.
clusters.risks: Rules must not widen owner-plane ACLs.

clusters.name: Automated reviewer and safety monitor for agent actions
clusters.description: A separate reviewer model approves eligible actions instead of asking the user every time, and a server-side monitor can pause runs that seem to misread instructions. (Supported only by DOC/INF records.)

bestInClass.why: Only source (DOC only, q4/q3); internals undocumented.

clusters.mechanism: Policy marks some ask-class actions as auto-reviewable; a reviewer model evaluates the action against the goal and constraints; approve, escalate to user, or block; monitor runs on the trajectory and can pause.

verevon.gap: No reviewer or monitor model found in the baseline; approvals are human-only or policy Allow with signed evidence.

clusters.benefit: Reduces approval fatigue on long Do runs without widening authority.
clusters.approach: Reviewer may only downgrade Ask to Allow for capabilities an admin marks reviewable, and must never override Deny; record the review in the audit trail.
clusters.risks: Model-approved effects; must be audited and scoped; DOC-only evidence.
clusters.rationale: Interesting but evidence is DOC-only and it touches the authority model.

clusters.name: Persistent goals with auto-continuation
clusters.description: The user sets an objective (with optional success criteria and token budget); the agent keeps working across turns until a judge or audit decides it is complete, blocked or out of budget.

bestInClass.why: Codex (q5) persists ThreadGoal with token budget and an audited completion; Hermes uses an auxiliary judge with quality gates; DeepSeek shows a goal bar with compare-and-set edits.

clusters.mechanism: Goal{objective, success_criteria, token_budget, used, status active|completed|blocked|cancelled}; when the run goes idle a continuation driver re-prompts with goal state; a cheap judge model checks completion against criteria with evidence; stop on budget or blocker and notify.

verevon.gap: No goal primitive found (SRC grep for goal state/thread goal: none; 'goal' only names the run's bound task). Long autonomous work is also bounded by the 300 s delegated bearer (OD8) and 4 default rounds.
verevon.strengths: Agent Run Console already has a goal launcher UI that could host it.

clusters.benefit: Core to the Manus/ChatGPT Work vision of outcome agents that work for a long time.
clusters.approach: Goal record in session-core; continuation driver as a Temporal workflow (orchestrator-core) that starts budgeted Do runs until the judge (verevon-balance) passes; requires a renewable delegated credential.
clusters.risks: Runaway cost; must re-check authority each continuation (Control reauthorizer).
clusters.rationale: Present in 6 sources and central to long-running agent work.

clusters.name: Subagent delegation and lifecycle
clusters.description: The main agent spawns child agents with isolated context, waits for or resumes them, and reads their results, with durable lineage.

bestInClass.why: Codex multi-agent v2 (q5) has task-path addressing and wait/resume/interrupt; Cursor's Task tool (q5) supports custom and background subagents; Hermes records async delegations durably with honest unknown outcomes.

clusters.mechanism: Tool subagent.task{goal, role, model?, tools?} creates a child run with a fresh LoopContext, parent_run_id and task path; the child budget is drawn atomically from the parent; the conclusion is persisted on the child run; the parent reads it with read_subagent_result; a background variant returns a handle and the parent is woken on completion instead of polling.

verevon.gap: Synchronous delegation within a turn is shipped with durable lineage and cold-resume read-back. Weaker: depth 1, no background/async children (FIFO inbox not adopted by decision), and lineage is shown only in the plan panel.
verevon.strengths: Durable child runs, consent-gated read-back, cold resume and an org-overridable child ceiling. Keep the fresh-context contract.

clusters.benefit: Parity for research fan-out; async children would enable long parallel work.
clusters.approach: Keep synchronous delegation; revisit async children only together with goals (C34).
clusters.risks: Async children multiply cost and authority surface.
clusters.rationale: Verevon is at parity on the core mechanic.

clusters.name: Delegation governance: authorization, depth, concurrency and model policy
clusters.description: Rules for when the model may delegate, depth and concurrency caps, per-subagent model policy and tool denial for leaf agents.

bestInClass.why: Codex (q5) forbids delegation unless explicitly asked; Cursor governs subagent models by policy; DeepSeek persists depth across cold resume.

clusters.mechanism: Server-side caps {max_depth, max_children_total, max_concurrent} resolved per org; leaf agents get a denied tool set (no further delegation, no risky effects); model policy inherit|forced|blocked; a prompt rule that depth or thoroughness alone is not a reason to delegate.

verevon.gap: Depth 1, a child ceiling of 8/100 with org override and the leaf restriction on risky calls are shipped. No per-subagent model policy found in the baseline.
verevon.strengths: The leaf restriction and atomic shared budget match the best sources.

clusters.benefit: Already strong.
clusters.approach: Add an optional per-role model policy when custom roles land (C07c).
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Custom agent roles and definitions
clusters.description: Users or plugins define named agents (description, prompt, tools, model, permission mode) in config files that the main agent can delegate to.

bestInClass.why: Cursor's .cursor/agents markdown files carry tools, model and permission mode; Codex validates roles and rejects duplicates.

clusters.mechanism: Agent definition record {name, description, instructions, tool_allowlist, model_policy, autonomy_cap} stored per Space/org with ownership; exposed to the delegation tool as selectable roles; the capability gate still applies per call.

verevon.gap: Preset agents exist but have empty action sets; agent installations are read-only; blueprint roles are design previews.

clusters.benefit: Turns the Agents page into something users configure; needed for the agent-pages vision.
clusters.approach: Store role definitions in the Model Plane (capability-core registry), bind tool allowlists to capability ids, and let subagent.task accept a role id.
clusters.risks: A role must never grant more than the owner-plane ACL (Space access never widens).
clusters.rationale: Agent pages are in product scope and are currently stubs.

clusters.name: Structured subagent and run results
clusters.description: Callers supply a JSON schema and the child or run reports its final answer through a reserved terminal tool or a post-run extraction step.

bestInClass.why: DeepSeek (q4, SRC) registers a child-scoped structured_output tool with a guard so the run cannot reopen; Manus extracts against a strict schema subset.

clusters.mechanism: Optional output_schema on subagent.task; register a structured_output tool whose arguments are validated against the schema; calling it concludes the child; the parent receives typed {status, summary, evidence, next_steps, blocker}.

verevon.gap: The typed handoff report is deferred by decision until code must branch on outcomes.

clusters.benefit: Needed once orchestration (C11/C12) branches on child outcomes.
clusters.approach: Build together with C11; reuse mp-contracts tool_arguments validation.
clusters.risks: Low.
clusters.rationale: Deferred by decision with a clear trigger.

clusters.name: Cache-preserving fork subagent
clusters.description: A child inherits the parent's completed turns and model so its copied history hits the provider prompt cache.

bestInClass.why: Only source (q5, SRC).

clusters.mechanism: Seed the child with a balanced completed-turn prefix of the parent and the same provider/model/tools so the prefix is cache-identical; mark inherited turns; close with reason 'forked'.

verevon.gap: Rejected by decision 2026-08-24 (fresh-context contract). Note: the ledger says DeepSeek rejected it, while the DeepSeek record shows an in-process fork tool; check which is current.
verevon.strengths: Fresh-context isolation is a deliberate safety property.

clusters.benefit: Lower cost for many small forks, but it conflicts with Verevon's isolation contract.
clusters.approach: Do not build.
clusters.risks: Leaks parent context into children with different authority.
clusters.rationale: Contradicts an owner decision; the benefit is cost only.

clusters.name: Inter-agent messaging (mailbox, message board, cross-session envelopes)
clusters.description: Agents and sessions send prioritised messages to each other with delivery timing, escaped sender envelopes and permission-parity guards.

bestInClass.why: Claude (q5) adds permission-class parity and escaped envelopes so a less privileged session cannot steer a more privileged one; Antigravity has priority and delivery strategy.

clusters.mechanism: Message{sender, recipient, priority, delivery NEXT_INVOCATION|WHEN_IDLE, content}; the receiver gets a wrapped, escaped envelope marked as non-instruction data; hold or refuse when the sender's autonomy is higher than the receiver's policy allows.

verevon.gap: Not adopted by decision: delegation is synchronous within a turn.

clusters.benefit: Only needed with async/background agents.
clusters.approach: Revisit with C34/C11; if built, adopt Claude's permission-parity guard.
clusters.risks: Prompt injection between agents; authority laundering.
clusters.rationale: Out of scope until async multi-agent exists.

clusters.name: Agent-driven session and task management
clusters.description: The model can list, search, create, message, stop and archive the user's other sessions or tasks, with a fan-out cap on agent-started sessions.

bestInClass.why: Claude (q5) exposes cross-session tools with one approval card and a per-user-message fan-out budget.

clusters.mechanism: Tools list_threads/search_threads/send_to_thread/stop_run scoped to the caller's own threads; starts are counted against a budget since the last user message, and an approval is required beyond it.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Check whether any model tool can read or start other threads (server-side search is absent).

clusters.benefit: Enables 'tidy my chats' and agent-started follow-up tasks.
clusters.approach: Later: expose thread tools through the Model Plane with tenant scoping and a fan-out cap.
clusters.risks: Cross-thread data mixing; must respect Space ACLs.

clusters.name: Multi-agent orchestration patterns (coordinator, teams, swarms, project mode)
clusters.description: A coordinator agent that only plans and delegates to parallel workers, with phase gates, shared progress files and synthesis.

bestInClass.why: Cursor Project mode (q4, SRC) is a non-editing orchestrator with phase gates and a single-writer progress file; Antigravity has pipelines and swarms; Perplexity Computer is the closest web benchmark.

clusters.mechanism: Coordinator run with no effect tools; it writes a plan, spawns a worker per item (bounded concurrency), collects structured results, runs a verifier pass, then synthesizes; progress lives in one single-writer record; a fresh successor coordinator per milestone avoids context rot.

verevon.gap: Team/coordinator mode is an in-memory gRPC stub; Temporal WideResearch/DeepTask workflows exist, but chat and Do do not use them.
verevon.strengths: Temporal-backed durable workflows exist and could host this.

clusters.benefit: Matches Perplexity Computer and Manus Wide Research for research-heavy tasks.
clusters.approach: Run coordinator mode as a Temporal workflow in orchestrator-core that reuses subagent.task for workers; expose it as a Do-mode option.
clusters.risks: Cost blow-up; needs fan-out confirmation (C12).
clusters.rationale: A strong differentiator, but it depends on structured results and cost controls.

clusters.name: Model-authored orchestration workflows
clusters.description: The model writes a deterministic script that fans work out to subagents, with a confirmation card for large fan-outs and a phase view of the run.

bestInClass.why: The Manus Workflow Composer (q5, DOC) is deterministic and replayable and powers Wide Research; Manus asks for confirmation above about 20 agent calls.

clusters.mechanism: The model emits a script for a sandboxed, deterministic runtime (no I/O, no clock/random) that calls agent()/parallel(); the runtime estimates agent calls and requires user confirmation above a threshold; phases render as a rail in the UI.

verevon.gap: Temporal workflows exist but are not the production path; whether model-authored fan-out is wanted at all is an open decision.

clusters.benefit: Powerful for wide research but overlaps C11.
clusters.approach: Decide C11 first; if adopted, compile the script to a Temporal workflow behind a cost-estimate card.
clusters.risks: Determinism and cost; open owner decision.
clusters.rationale: Open decision; C11 covers most of the value.

clusters.name: Code mode / programmatic tool calling
clusters.description: The model writes a script (JS or Python) that calls tools as functions inside a sandbox, collapsing multi-step tool chains into one step with resource budgets.

bestInClass.why: Codex (q5) runs model JS in a fresh V8 isolate with tools as async functions; Manus (q5) adds per-cell budgets and resumable state.

clusters.mechanism: exec(source) runs in an isolate with no filesystem or network; tools are injected as async functions that go back through the normal capability gate; per-cell limits {native calls, output bytes, timeout, heap}; a state object persists across cells.

verevon.gap: Not built (BKL #11); code_interpreter exists but cannot call Verevon tools.

clusters.benefit: Fewer rounds and tokens for data-heavy Do tasks; fits inside the 4-round default.
clusters.approach: Add a tool bridge in sandbox-manager so code_interpreter can call capability-gated tools through execution-core; every call still passes EvaluatePolicy.
clusters.risks: Gate bypass if the bridge is not routed through execution-core.
clusters.rationale: High leverage for agent efficiency; already planned.

clusters.name: Best-of-N and multi-model synthesis
clusters.description: Run one prompt as several parallel attempts (different models or seeds), compare, then pick a winner or merge the answers.

bestInClass.why: Antigravity Battle Mode (q5) forks into isolated clones with elimination and a winner; Cursor synthesizes one answer from per-model subagents.

clusters.mechanism: Fan out N child runs with different models; collect the results; either the user picks a winner or a synthesis step merges them; show the cost before start.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; the baseline narrative notes no model comparison in chat. Check for any multi-model compare path.

clusters.benefit: Answer quality for hard questions; multi-model is a stated goal (T3 Code reference).
clusters.approach: Reuse subagent fan-out with one model per child and a synthesis prompt.
clusters.risks: Cost multiplication.

clusters.name: Background commands and jobs with await and notifications
clusters.description: Long-running commands move to the background; the agent awaits them or is notified on completion or on matching output.

bestInClass.why: Cursor (q5) moves commands to the background after a timeout and supports output-pattern notifications; DeepSeek scopes jobs to the starting agent with a wake budget.

clusters.mechanism: process_start returns a handle after block_until_ms; a registry keeps a rolling buffer; await(handle, timeout) and notify_on_output{pattern, debounce} wake the agent with a completion notice; jobs are owned by the starting run and cancelled with it.

verevon.gap: process_* tools exist for Space-scoped runs (lease with space:processes); there is no notify-on-output wake of the agent, and they are not available outside Spaces.
verevon.strengths: bwrap isolation and lease-gated access.

clusters.benefit: Needed for long data jobs in Do mode.
clusters.approach: Add await and output-pattern watches through the S4.3 Watch primitive's process adapter.
clusters.risks: Runaway processes; quotas.
clusters.rationale: Partly there; it mostly matters for coding-style tasks.

clusters.name: Background work and subagent fleet panel
clusters.description: A UI panel or banner that lists running and finished subagents, background jobs and workflows for the current task, with per-item output and stop controls.

bestInClass.why: T3 Code (q4, SRC) turns provider task events into a 'Kicked off N subagents' row and a lifecycle banner with Stop; Claude adds a task backlog; Manus has per-job stop.

clusters.mechanism: Map run/child-run/process events to task.* rows {id, kind, title, status, started_at, output_ref}; render a collapsible fleet panel and a banner above the composer ('3 agents working', Stop all); confirm before stopping work that cannot be resumed.

verevon.gap: The Work panel and Agent Run Console show the timeline, but subagent lineage is fetched only for the plan panel and the fleet console calls /v1/fleets with no gateway route (stub).
verevon.strengths: Work panel answers 'what is happening / does Verevon need you' with live telemetry.

clusters.benefit: Users can see and stop parallel work; needed once C11 lands.
clusters.approach: Frontend: a fleet section in the Work panel fed by child-run events already in the run event stream; add the gateway route for fleets.
clusters.risks: Low.
clusters.rationale: Cheap visibility win on top of shipped events.

clusters.name: Scheduled agent runs (cron/RRULE) with result delivery
clusters.description: Recurring or one-time tasks run as full agent runs (tools, skills, model choice) on a schedule, locally or in the cloud, with run history and results delivered to an inbox, notification or channel.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q5) runs cron jobs as full agent runs with scripts, skills, context chaining, multi-platform delivery and an at-most-once ledger; Claude (q5) adds GitHub-event and API triggers; Manus (q5) has a rich schedule model with expiry and run target.

clusters.mechanism: Schedule{rrule|cron, tz, prompt, model, skills, autonomy_cap, run_target new_thread|same_thread, expiry}; sweeper claims slots at-most-once with catch-up windows; each slot starts a normal budgeted Do run; result summary lands in an inbox with read state and a notification; incidents and quota holds recorded.

verevon.gap: A cron sweeper and Temporal ScheduledRunSupervision exist, but each scheduled step is one no-tool 1,024-token call on verevon-balance, owner ruling 2026-09-28 makes scheduled runs draft-only, and no result delivery ('Se resultater') is wired.
verevon.strengths: Durable Temporal supervision already exists.

clusters.benefit: Users expect 'every Monday, summarise my inbox' to actually use tools; present in 10 of 12 sources.
clusters.approach: Make ExecuteScheduledStep start a governed Do run with a pre-approved autonomy cap set at schedule time (draft-only effects allowed by the owner ruling), deliver results via notification-core and an inbox view.
clusters.risks: Unattended effects; must stay draft-only until the owner revisits; authority re-checked per run.
clusters.rationale: Table-stakes capability shipped only as a stub.

clusters.name: Event- and webhook-triggered automations
clusters.description: Agents start on external events (new email, Slack message, calendar event, GitHub PR, CI, webhook) with filters (sometimes LLM-evaluated), revisions and execution history; agents can also subscribe to events and go idle until they fire.

bestInClass.why: Cursor (q5, SRC) has a 42-method automations service with event triggers, LLM filtering and deploy specs; Manus (q5, DOC) has a trigger catalog with revisions, dry runs and execution history; Cursor agents can subscribe to timers/PRs instead of polling.

clusters.mechanism: Trigger{source provider+event, filter (structured + optional LLM predicate), prompt template, run_target, revision}; provider webhooks normalized by the integration layer into events; dedupe and rate-limit; each match starts a budgeted run; execution log with dry-run.

verevon.gap: No event-trigger record in the baseline. The S4.3 Watch primitive (cursor-bearing, authority re-checked at disclosure) is partial and only has a process-output adapter; bridge-core has a webhook channel adapter that is not a trigger system.
verevon.strengths: Watch primitive re-checks authority at disclosure time, which is the right safety shape.

clusters.benefit: Event-driven agents (reply drafts on new mail, ticket triage) are where Manus, ChatGPT Tasks and Perplexity are heading.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane (integration-corev2) emits normalized provider events to NATS; capability-core trigger records subscribe and start Do runs; Model Plane never polls providers directly.
clusters.risks: Cross-plane: provider events belong to Ingestion; event floods; prompt injection from inbound mail must be treated as data.
clusters.rationale: Strong user value but depends on scheduled runs working first.

clusters.name: Automation run state and wake gates
clusters.description: Each automation keeps a small notepad or memory file across runs, can skip the model entirely when a cheap source has not changed, and stays silent when there is nothing to report.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q5) hashes a monitor source and only wakes the agent on change, supports a wake gate and a silent sentinel, and keeps a per-job notepad; Codex requires a one-line inbox summary per run.

clusters.mechanism: Per-schedule state {notepad kv, last_source_hash, cursor}; pre-run probe (URL/script/provider query) whose SHA-256 is compared with the last triggering hash; unchanged means a no-op run with no model call; the agent can end with a silent sentinel; the notepad is injected into the prompt and updated by a tool.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; scheduled runs are a single no-tool call without state.

clusters.benefit: Monitoring automations become cheap and non-spammy (Verevon Balance cost model).
clusters.approach: Add notepad and probe fields to capability-core schedules; probes executed via Ingestion (Quarry) or integration-corev2, never by the model directly.
clusters.risks: Probe execution must respect plane ownership (Quarry executes).

clusters.name: Automation authoring and sharing UX
clusters.description: Automations are authored from typed blueprints rendered as form, slash command and agent prompt; run history rows offer 'ask AI why it failed'; task definitions can be shared or run under a team account.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q4) defines one slot schema that renders everywhere; Manus offers AI triage of failed or dropped runs; ChatGPT shares task definitions as independent copies.

clusters.mechanism: Blueprint{key, schedule_template, prompt_template, slots[time|enum|text|weekdays]}; fill validates slots and produces a schedule; failed runs get an 'explain' action that starts a read-only run over the run log; share exports the definition, not credentials.

verevon.gap: 'Schedule this' dialog and /schedule exist; no blueprints, failure triage or sharing.

clusters.benefit: Lowers the barrier to automations for non-technical users.
clusters.approach: Frontend blueprints backed by capability-core schedule specs; triage reuses a read-only Ask run.
clusters.risks: Shared definitions must not carry the author's grants.

clusters.name: Consent-first proactive suggestions
clusters.description: The agent proposes ready-to-run automations, next tasks or configuration changes as cards the user accepts or dismisses, with deduplication and caps.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q4) stores suggestions with a dedup latch, a pending cap of 5 and one-tap accept; Codex generates ambient suggestions from projects and apps.

clusters.mechanism: Suggestion{source, spec, dedup_key, status pending|accepted|dismissed}; generated post-turn or from usage; accept calls the normal create path under user authority.

verevon.gap: No baseline record.

clusters.benefit: Helps users discover automations; supports the 'learns its user' reference (Hermes).
clusters.approach: After C35a: post-turn suggestion pass writing pending suggestions to session-core; Frontend cards.
clusters.risks: Annoyance; must be capped and dismissable.

clusters.name: Persistent named personal agents
clusters.description: Long-lived agents with their own identity (name, avatar, instructions, memory, skills, sometimes email, phone or a cloud computer) that keep working between conversations and can join group chats with humans and other agents.

bestInClass.why: Manus (q4, SRC) ships named agents with their own email, phone, computer and skills; Codex's hidden 'aeon' assistant and ChatGPT Dots show OpenAI moving the same way; Hermes builds bots from profiles.

clusters.mechanism: Agent{id, owner, persona, instructions, memory scope, skills, channels[], autonomy_cap}; a permanent main thread per agent; inbound messages from channels start runs on that thread; schedules and goals attach to the agent.

verevon.gap: Agents overview has role blueprints labelled as design previews; agent installations are read-only reads of Space agent installations; no persistent agent identity with its own thread or channels.
verevon.strengths: Space agent installations give a server-side anchor to build on.

clusters.benefit: Defines what the Agents page is; strong differentiation against plain chat.
clusters.approach: Model a persistent agent as a Space agent installation plus a main thread in session-core, with memory scoped to the agent; channels later via the Channel Plane.
clusters.risks: Identity and ACL: an agent must act with the owner's delegated, never widened, authority.
clusters.rationale: Direction of the market and of Verevon's agent pages; large effort.

clusters.name: Workspace agent builder and deployment surfaces
clusters.description: Business users build an agent from a prompt or template, preview it, version it, pick model and connectors, and deploy it to Slack, schedules or an API trigger with an activity log.

bestInClass.why: ChatGPT Workspace Agents (q4, DOC) with versions, schedules, Slack and API trigger; the Codex bundle shows the Slack and activity-log implementation (SRC).

clusters.mechanism: Builder UI producing a versioned agent spec {instructions, model, connectors with per-action ask policy, triggers}; preview runs in a sandbox thread; publish creates a deployment with an activity log of runs.

verevon.gap: Workflow builder and Chatbot studio are design previews; the Agent Run Console can launch goals but there is no saved, versioned agent spec.
verevon.strengths: Agent Run Console (timeline, approvals, proof bundle) is a solid run view to reuse.

clusters.benefit: Turns Verevon agent pages into a product for teams.
clusters.approach: Versioned agent specs in capability-core; builder in Frontend; deployments reuse schedules (C35a) and triggers (C35c).
clusters.risks: Connector write actions must default to always-ask.
clusters.rationale: Agent pages are in scope; reuse existing console.

clusters.name: Agent entry points beyond the app (email, Slack, Teams, issue trackers)
clusters.description: Users start or continue agent tasks by emailing an agent address, mentioning it in Slack/Teams, or from issue trackers; replies come back in-thread.

bestInClass.why: Perplexity (q4, DOC) runs Computer from forwarded email with the sender's permissions and binds Slack channels to projects; Manus (SRC) creates tasks by email with allowlists.

clusters.mechanism: Inbound adapter per channel normalizes messages to {sender identity, thread ref, content, attachments}; sender mapped to a Verevon user and checked against an allowlist; a run starts with origin=channel; output delivered by the platform tool, not as chat text.

verevon.gap: Baseline narrative: bridge-core has a session registry, webhook channel adapter and delivery worker; the Channel Plane is docs-only/future.

clusters.benefit: Meets users where they work; differentiator for business users.
clusters.approach: Wait for the Channel Plane; keep Model Plane runs origin-aware (C46) so channels can plug in later.
clusters.risks: Inbound content is untrusted data (prompt injection); identity spoofing on email.
clusters.rationale: Channel Plane is explicitly future; prepare, do not build now.

clusters.name: Server-side runs that continue after the client closes, with parallel tasks
clusters.description: Tasks run on the provider's servers, keep going when the page or laptop is closed, and several can run in parallel with per-plan concurrency limits.

bestInClass.why: Claude web (q5, DOC) keeps sessions running with idle VM snapshots; Manus gives each task its own VM with plan-based concurrency.

clusters.mechanism: Runs are owned by the server; the client only subscribes; resume via event ids; concurrency limit per plan enforced at admission.

verevon.gap: Durable runs with replay and 'notify me when done' are shipped. Not verified: per-plan concurrency limits at admission.
verevon.strengths: Verevon is a web product: runs are server-side by construction, with durable replay and background-run notifications.

clusters.benefit: Keep.
clusters.approach: Add plan-based concurrency limits via Control-plane entitlements if missing.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Cloud coding environments as code (repo VMs, PR delivery, self-hosted workers)
clusters.description: Coding agents run in cloud VMs built from a repository environment spec, deliver pull requests, and can run on self-hosted worker pools.

bestInClass.why: Cursor (q5) has pods, snapshots, environment-as-code and a self-hosted worker daemon.

clusters.mechanism: environment.json/Dockerfile per repo; setup agent; pod snapshots; worker daemon claims jobs from a pool; delivery as PR.

verevon.gap: Not applicable as such: Verevon is not an IDE. Sandboxes exist (sandbox-manager, bwrap, Space leases) for code execution.

clusters.benefit: Low for Verevon's chat/agent pages.
clusters.approach: Skip; keep sandbox-manager for code execution and documents.
clusters.risks: Scope creep into IDE territory.
clusters.rationale: Out of product scope (Verevon is not an IDE).

clusters.name: Cross-device continuation of a live task
clusters.description: A task started on one device can be monitored, answered and redirected from another (phone, web), with push notifications when input is needed.

bestInClass.why: Claude (q4, DOC) lets users answer questions and redirect from mobile with push; Claude Desktop Dispatch (SRC) applies unattended-turn policy to phone-started sessions.

clusters.mechanism: Server-owned runs plus resumable streams; notifications on awaiting_input/approval; any device can submit decisions or queued input against the run id.

verevon.gap: Server-side runs, stream resume and notifications exist; push to a mobile device and answering approvals from notifications were not verified.
verevon.strengths: Web-first architecture gives this nearly for free.

clusters.benefit: Keep; add push when a mobile surface exists.
clusters.approach: Route awaiting_approval/awaiting_input to notification-core with deep links.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Local machine bridge (remote control, SSH, keep-awake, local-to-cloud teleport)
clusters.description: Desktop apps expose local folders or SSH hosts so sessions started elsewhere run on the user's machine, survive disconnects, keep the machine awake, and can be teleported to the cloud.

bestInClass.why: Claude Desktop (q5, SRC) serves trusted folders as remote environments, keeps SSH sessions alive across disconnects with sequence replay, and moves local sessions to the cloud.

clusters.mechanism: Local helper registers folders as environments; a remote helper daemon runs the engine and buffers events by sequence; on reconnect replay from the last sequence; keep-awake claims while runs are active.

verevon.gap: Not applicable today: Verevon is a web app without a desktop agent.

clusters.benefit: Only if Verevon ships a desktop companion for computer use (Manus My Computer style).
clusters.approach: Skip for now; revisit with the computer-use category.
clusters.risks: Large security surface on user machines.

clusters.name: Workspace and file checkpoints with revert
clusters.description: Before each turn the files the agent may change are snapshotted (often in a shadow git store); the user can revert to any message, undo the revert, and deliverables keep versions.

bestInClass.why: T3 Code (q4, SRC) snapshots the tree into hidden git refs via a temporary index and coordinates revert across files, provider and refs; Claude adds undo-rewind and fork.

clusters.mechanism: Per turn: snapshot touched files into a content-addressed store; record checkpoint{turn_id, refs}; revert restores files and truncates the conversation consistently; effectful provider writes are marked non-rewindable.

verevon.gap: No user-facing checkpoint or rewind (I11 planned); artifacts have versions by re-emitting ids; recommended scope OD19: conversation plus artifact versions, effectful turns non-rewindable.
verevon.strengths: Artifact versions already exist; 'effectful turns are immutable' is a sound rule.

clusters.benefit: Undo for agent edits to artifacts and Space documents.
clusters.approach: Implement OD19: checkpoint artifact versions and Space file revisions per turn (Data Plane owns documents; Model Plane records references only).
clusters.risks: Cross-plane: the Model Plane must not write Data Plane stores directly.
clusters.rationale: Valuable, but documents live in another plane and C40b gives most of the user value.

clusters.name: Conversation rewind, fork and side chats
clusters.description: A chat can be rolled back N turns, reverted, forked at a turn boundary, or branched into a throwaway side conversation that returns to the parent.

bestInClass.why: Codex (q5) has rollback, revert, fork lineage and undo; Cursor (q5) stores conversation state as content-addressed blobs so any checkpoint is resumable.

clusters.mechanism: Thread history as immutable turns with parent pointers; fork creates a new thread referencing turns up to a boundary (copy-on-write); rewind moves the head pointer; side chat is a child thread whose result can be inserted back.

verevon.gap: No server branch model (sessions.proto has no branch fields; parent_message_id = 21 unused); only a client-side 'Fortsett i ny chat' and client-only edit siblings that vanish on reload.

clusters.benefit: Table-stakes chat feature (ChatGPT, Claude); users notice when edits lose history.
clusters.approach: Add parent_message_id and branch head to session-core threads; fork/rewind RPCs; effectful turns non-rewindable.
clusters.risks: ZDR threads cannot be forked server-side.

clusters.name: Agent status machine, turn attribution and origins
clusters.description: Each thread or task exposes a small status set (idle, active, waiting on approval, waiting on input, error) with elapsed-work indicators, and records who started each turn and from which surface.

bestInClass.why: Codex (q4) reports thread status with waiting-on-approval/input and turn attribution by source; Manus shows 'Working for {duration}'.

clusters.mechanism: ThreadStatus{not_loaded|idle|active{waiting_on_approval, waiting_on_input}|error}; turn{kind, origin web|schedule|channel|subagent|api, started_by}; UI badges and elapsed timers.

verevon.gap: Work panel answers whether Verevon needs you and threads carry an origin filter; a unified status enum and turn attribution by origin were not verified.
verevon.strengths: Work panel lifecycle and live telemetry.

clusters.benefit: Needed once scheduled, triggered and channel runs exist (C35a/C35c/C37).
clusters.approach: Add origin and started_by to run records in session-core; expose status on thread lists.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Next-prompt suggestions
clusters.description: After a turn the product suggests the user's likely next prompt or follow-up questions.

bestInClass.why: Only source in this category (q3, SRC).

clusters.mechanism: Post-answer cheap inference produces short follow-up lines emitted as a typed event.

verevon.gap: Baseline narrative: follow-up suggestions are shipped (follow_ups event).
verevon.strengths: Shipped and sanitised.

clusters.benefit: Keep.
clusters.approach: None.
clusters.risks: None.

clusters.name: Outcome verification before delivery
clusters.description: The agent follows an operating contract to plan testing, verify outcomes (for example test a generated app in a browser) and stop at sufficient evidence before declaring success.

bestInClass.why: Manus (q4, SRC) ships an observe-plan-batch-verify playbook; Cursor's cloud-agent contract requires test planning and evidence.

clusters.mechanism: Written operating contract in the prompt plus a verification step: after effects, run checks and attach evidence to the final message.

verevon.gap: Deterministic postcondition verifiers and a Verified Outcome/Proof Bundle are shipped; no type-check feedback for run_code and no automatic re-fetch for Visma.
verevon.strengths: Deterministic read-back verification of provider writes is stronger than prompt-only playbooks. Keep.

clusters.benefit: Keep.
clusters.approach: Extend verifiers to more providers.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: UI actions and scripts compiled into agent turns
clusters.description: Buttons in the UI (commit, create automation, investigate a run) produce templated, machine-readable agent turns; a scripted prelude can run tool calls before the first model call.

bestInClass.why: Cursor (q4) maps simulated-message reasons to templates; Manus automation screens send the agent structured requests.

clusters.mechanism: Action registry maps a UI action to a template {reason, parameters}; the gateway renders a structured user turn; optional prelude executes deterministic tool calls and feeds results to the model.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Check src/shared/actions (typed actions shared by UI and agents) for templated-turn generation.

clusters.benefit: One code path for UI and agent actions; aligns with Verevon's typed action API goal.
clusters.approach: Add a templated-turn renderer in the gateway keyed by action ids.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Multi-agent write isolation
clusters.description: Parallel agents get their own worktrees or a cross-agent file-state registry, and a pre-final barrier checks whether shared state changed underneath an agent.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q4) offers opt-in worktrees and a process-wide registry against overwrites; Cursor injects a conflict barrier before finishing.
