clusters.mechanism: Per-child worktree or a registry of file versions read/written per agent; refuse writes based on stale reads; barrier before final answer.

verevon.gap: Replaced by decision with a per-run child ceiling; children do not write shared files in parallel.

clusters.benefit: Low under synchronous delegation.
clusters.approach: Skip; revisit if async children write Space files.
clusters.risks: None now.

clusters.name: Atomic run bootstrap saga
clusters.description: The first message of a new thread runs one server-side transaction (create thread, prepare workspace, run setup, start turn) that rolls back on failure.

bestInClass.why: T3 Code (q4) runs a bootstrap program with rollback; DeepSeek awaits agent creation as one rollback-capable transaction.

clusters.mechanism: Saga with compensations: create thread -> prepare workspace -> start turn; on failure undo previous steps and return one error.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Check the gateway's prepared-run path for partial-failure cleanup.

clusters.benefit: Low.
clusters.approach: Verify; add compensations if threads leak on failed starts.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Post-turn background learning passes
clusters.description: After a turn is delivered, a background fork reviews the conversation and writes memory or skills; an idle-time curator archives stale skills; foreground turns always pre-empt the review.

bestInClass.why: Only source (Hermes, q4): review fork shares the cached prefix, runs under a tool whitelist, and is cancelled by any new user turn.

clusters.mechanism: On turn delivery enqueue a review job with a snapshot; run it with memory/skill tools only; cancel on new foreground activity (ABA-safe run token); an idle curator ranks skills by usage and archives, never deletes.

verevon.gap: MemoryConsolidation, SkillPromotion and FeedbackPromotion Temporal workflows exist but are started only by capability-core's task executor; no post-turn review fork wired to chat (see memory category).
verevon.strengths: Durable workflows for promotion already exist.

clusters.benefit: Supports the Hermes reference goal (learns and tailors itself to its user).
clusters.approach: Trigger SkillPromotion/MemoryConsolidation after non-ZDR turns via NATS events; enforce a tool whitelist and pre-emption.
clusters.risks: ZDR: never run on ZDR turns; skill poisoning from untrusted content.
clusters.rationale: Key to the Hermes-style learning goal; overlaps the memory category.

clusters.name: Emergency stop and maintenance fence
clusters.description: An operator or admin can pause all new agent work (cron, dispatch, new turns) without killing in-flight work, and safe restarts wait for idleness.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q4) pauses new work install-wide through a fail-safe sentinel; Manus reports idleness and fences maintenance.

clusters.mechanism: Global or org-level pause flag checked at admission for runs, schedules and triggers; activity status {active turns, in-flight actions}; maintenance begins when idle.

verevon.gap: Graceful drain on redeploy is shipped; no org-level or global pause of new agent work was found.
verevon.strengths: Drain with /readyz 503 and in-flight completion.

clusters.benefit: Enterprise admins and incident response can stop agents fast.
clusters.approach: Control-plane org flag 'agents paused' checked by capability-core admission and the gateway.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Thread lifecycle housekeeping (settle, snooze, utility-model titles, deletion cascade)
clusters.description: Threads are settled or snoozed manually or automatically, a cheap utility model writes titles and summaries, and deleting a thread cascades to its sessions and terminals.

bestInClass.why: Only source (T3 Code, q5 settle/snooze with client/server invariants).

clusters.mechanism: effectiveSettled computed from activity blockers, overrides and inactivity; utility model per provider for titles; deletion reactor stops sessions.

verevon.gap: Baseline narrative: auto titles, archive and durable delete are shipped; no settle/snooze.
verevon.strengths: Durable erase contract on delete.

clusters.benefit: Low.
clusters.approach: Optional snooze for background runs later.
clusters.risks: None.

clusters.name: Warm session caching and idle reaping
clusters.description: Agent processes or VMs stay warm for a grace period between turns and are reaped when idle, without killing active turns or background work.

bestInClass.why: T3 Code (q4) reaps idle provider sessions only when no turn or background work is live; Hermes evicts warm agents by RSS.

clusters.mechanism: Track last_seen per session; sweep periodically; skip sessions with active turns or background liveness; evict LRU under memory pressure.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Check sandbox-manager idle policies; Verevon's loop is stateless per request, so this mainly matters for sandboxes.

clusters.benefit: Low.
clusters.approach: Skip unless sandbox start latency becomes a problem.
clusters.risks: Low.

clusters.name: Deterministic replay corpus and fault-injecting mock model
clusters.description: Recorded sessions replay through the real runtime without an API key, a scriptable mock model injects stalls, malformed chunks and rate limits, and CI enforces coverage and performance budgets.

bestInClass.why: DeepSeek (q5, SRC) replays recorded parent and subagent sessions through shipped profiles and has a seeded fault-injection mock server.

clusters.mechanism: Record model transcripts as fixtures; replay server returns them in call order; override sidecar injects failures; tests assert on the persisted world state, not mocks.

verevon.gap: eval-lab-py has 14 offline YAML cases and an SLO harness; no keyless replay corpus or fault-injecting mock model was found in the baseline.
verevon.strengths: Offline eval cases cover HITL, org isolation, ZDR and compaction.

clusters.benefit: Safer changes to the two loops (which were deliberately not unified).
clusters.approach: Add a recorded-transcript replay backend to inference-core for tests plus a fault-injection mode.
clusters.risks: Fixtures must contain no customer data.

clusters.name: Live A/B harnesses and eval hooks in the production loop
clusters.description: Behaviour changes are validated by running real agents from two pinned versions over graded tasks; the production loop carries eval overrides and trajectory export.

bestInClass.why: Hermes (q5) runs isolated two-arm A/B evaluations of tool-visibility and prompt changes; Cursor keeps eval overrides in the production runtime.

clusters.mechanism: For each (arm, model, task, rep) run the agent hermetically and grade; compare arms; production runtime accepts eval overrides (temperature, token limits) and writes trajectories.

verevon.gap: Trajectory recording is an in-memory ring buffer (not durable); ops quality page shows basic success rate and drift.

clusters.benefit: Evidence-based harness changes.
clusters.approach: Persist trajectories (non-ZDR only) and add an A/B runner to eval-lab-py.
clusters.risks: ZDR: never record ZDR turns.

clusters.name: Engine/host separation and pluggable execution location
clusters.description: The agent loop is a separate engine driven over a protocol, and where tools execute (local machine, VM, SSH host, cloud) is chosen per session or per task by need.

bestInClass.why: Claude (q5) uses a custom spawn function so one engine runs locally, in a VM or over SSH; Cursor runs the loop server-side and executes tools on the client or a cloud VM.

clusters.mechanism: Engine speaks a typed protocol; a spawn/transport seam selects the executor; routing picks the location from task needs (local folders, browser, connectors only).

verevon.gap: No baseline record. INF: Verevon already separates the loop (execution-core) from execution (sandbox-manager, Quarry for browser), which is the web-product form of this pattern.
verevon.strengths: Model proposes browser actions and Quarry executes them; sandboxes are leased.

clusters.benefit: Already structurally present.
clusters.approach: Skip as a feature; keep the plane separation.
clusters.risks: None.
clusters.rationale: Architecture already matches the web-product form.

clusters.name: External agent engines as backends
clusters.description: Other agent products (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor agent, OpenCode, ACP agents) are driven as engines or one-shot subagents behind one provider facade with a canonical event taxonomy.

bestInClass.why: T3 Code (q5) routes threads to adapters for five protocols and normalizes their events while keeping raw payloads; DeepSeek can delegate to Claude Code, Codex or ACP agents.

clusters.mechanism: Adapter per engine (SDK stdio, app-server JSON-RPC, ACP, HTTP); a facade binds each thread to an adapter with a resume cursor; all events mapped to a canonical taxonomy with the native payload preserved.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; Verevon's multi-model support is through inference-core providers, not external agent engines.

clusters.benefit: Could offer 'run this with Codex/Claude Code' in sandboxes, but duplicates Verevon's own governed loop.
clusters.approach: Skip; prefer native multi-model through inference-core so the capability gate always applies.
clusters.risks: External engines bypass the capability gate and ZDR guarantees.
clusters.rationale: Conflicts with the governed-loop authority model.

clusters.name: Domain workflow modes for code (debug mode, PR babysit, autonomous PR agent)
clusters.description: Built-in workflows that drive code-specific loops: hypothesis-driven debugging with instrumentation, keeping a PR merge-ready, and an autonomous PR reviewer that auto-applies fixes.

bestInClass.why: Only source (Cursor).

clusters.mechanism: Mode-specific prompts and tools (instrument, reproduce, compare logs; watch CI and review comments).

verevon.gap: Not applicable: Verevon is not an IDE.

clusters.benefit: Low.
clusters.approach: Skip.
clusters.risks: Scope creep.

clusters.name: Response comparison for preference data
clusters.description: A second model's answer is generated in the background or shown side by side so the user can state a preference, feeding training data.

bestInClass.why: Only source (q4, SRC); runs only when privacy mode allows training.

clusters.mechanism: After a turn optionally generate an alternate response under a privacy gate and time limit; show both; record preference.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; Verevon records implicit dissatisfaction from regenerate/edit (v-chat-agents-ui-080) instead.
verevon.strengths: Implicit dissatisfaction signals already capture feedback without extra cost.

clusters.benefit: Low; conflicts with ZDR defaults and doubles cost.
clusters.approach: Skip.
clusters.risks: Privacy and ZDR.
clusters.rationale: Training-data feature, not a user need.

clusters.name: Headless agent API/SDK and lifecycle webhooks
clusters.description: Developers start and stream agent sessions programmatically, register client tools, and receive lifecycle webhooks.

bestInClass.why: The OpenAI Agents API (q4, DOC) hosts the full harness with a selectable environment; Codex lets hosts register dynamic tools at thread start.

clusters.mechanism: Public API: POST /sessions{environment, tools[]}, POST /sessions/:id/messages, an SSE stream, and webhooks task.created/stopped/deleted carrying structured_output; same runtime as the web app.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Check the gateway for a public, token-authenticated runs API and webhooks.

clusters.benefit: B2B integrations; not needed for the chat/agent pages.
clusters.approach: Defer; later expose the existing /v1/runs through Control-plane API keys.
clusters.risks: Abuse; billing.
clusters.rationale: Not on the chat/agent page critical path.

clusters.name: Record and replay a demonstrated workflow as a skill
clusters.description: The user performs a workflow once with computer use and it is turned into a reusable skill. (Supported only by DOC/INF records.)

bestInClass.why: Only source (DOC only).

clusters.mechanism: Record UI interactions, convert to a SKILL.md-style procedure, replay through computer use.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; requires desktop computer use, which Verevon does not have.

clusters.benefit: Low until computer use exists.
clusters.approach: Skip; revisit with computer use (browser procedures in Quarry could be a web variant).
clusters.risks: Recording sensitive screens.
